g: Apposition around the subject
‘Yo, Pablo, prisionero de Cristo Jesús’ places Pablo and prisionero as appositive descriptions of yo before the verb me arrodillo.
e: por el bien de ustedes
Por el bien de is the fixed expression ‘for the sake of’ or ‘for the benefit of’; ustedes identifies the beneficiaries.

g: Enterarse de + noun phrase
‘Se han enterado del plan’ uses pronominal enterarse with de; del contracts de + el. The relative que later refers to el plan.
e: el plan de la gracia de Dios
Plan renders the idea of an entrusted administration here; de la gracia identifies what that commission concerns.

g: Clarification with es decir
Es decir introduces a reformulation of the preceding plan. In ‘me dio a conocer,’ dar a conocer means ‘to make known,’ with me as recipient.
e: como ya les escribí brevemente
Como means ‘as’ here, not ‘like.’ Ya marks the earlier writing, les identifies its recipients, and brevemente describes its limited extent.

g: Future + two linked infinitives
‘Podrán darse cuenta de que comprendo’ uses future podrán with infinitive darse; the following de que clause states what readers can recognize.
e: el misterio de Cristo
In this letter misterio is not a puzzle to solve but a plan disclosed by God; de Cristo specifies the plan's relation to Christ.

g: Se-passive with an indirect object
In ‘no se les dio a conocer’ and ‘se les ha revelado,’ se forms an impersonal/passive construction while les marks the human recipients.
e: por el Espíritu
Por introduces the agent or means of revelation. The phrase belongs to se les ha revelado, while a introduces the people receiving it.

g: Three parallel predicate nouns
After ‘que los gentiles son,’ beneficiarios, miembros, and participantes form a three-part series, each expanded by de-phrases.
e: mediante el evangelio
Mediante is the formal preposition ‘through’ or ‘by means of.’ It identifies the gospel as the means of participation in the promise.

g: Llegar a ser for a change of state
‘Llegué a ser servidor’ means ‘I became a servant.’ Llegar is preterite because the change is viewed as a completed event.
e: el regalo que Dios me dio
The relative que is the direct object of dio, while me is the indirect object: literally, ‘the gift that God gave to me.’

g: Aunque + indicative for an accepted fact
‘Aunque soy el más insignificante’ uses indicative soy because the speaker presents this assessment as a fact, not a hypothetical concession.
e: recibí esta gracia de predicar
Gracia is followed by de + infinitive to specify the granted task: ‘this grace of preaching.’ Recibí is a completed preterite.

g: Coordinated de + infinitive complements
‘Y de hacer entender’ continues the infinitive governed by gracia in the preceding verse, adding a second commissioned activity.
e: Dios, creador de todas las cosas
Creador de todas las cosas is an appositive title identifying Dios; the comma marks it as supplementary information.

g: El fin ... es que + subjunctive
‘El fin ... es que ... se dé a conocer’ states an intended outcome, so dar appears as subjunctive dé in a se-passive construction.
e: por medio de la iglesia
Por medio de means ‘through’ or ‘by means of.’ It identifies the church as the channel through which the wisdom is made known.

g: Reduced participial modifier
‘Realizado en Cristo Jesús’ is a past-participle phrase modifying propósito; realizado agrees with the masculine singular noun.
e: conforme a su eterno propósito
Conforme a means ‘in accordance with.’ Here it connects the preceding disclosure to God's eternal purpose.

g: Para + pronominal infinitive
‘Libertad y confianza para acercarnos’ uses para + infinitive to state what the freedom enables; nos attaches to acercar.
e: En él, mediante la fe
Two fronted phrases frame the statement: en él locates the privilege in Christ, and mediante la fe gives the means of access.

g: Pedir que + negative subjunctive
‘Les pido que no se desanimen’ uses subjunctive after a request. The reflexive pronoun remains before the conjugated verb.
e: son para ustedes un honor
Ser para alguien algo can assign significance: the sufferings ‘are an honor for you.’ Para ustedes identifies who receives that honor.

g: Reflexive morphology in me arrodillo
Arrodillarse is conjugated with its required pronoun: yo me arrodillo. The doubled ll represents the /y/ sound in most dialects.
e: delante del Padre
Delante de means ‘before’ in the sense of being in someone's presence; del contracts de + el before Padre.

g: De quien as a relative complement
‘De quien recibe nombre toda familia’ refers back to el Padre. The preposition de belongs to the expression recibir nombre de.
e: en el cielo y en la tierra
The repeated en creates balanced locations, ‘in heaven and on earth,’ and together gives the scope of toda familia.

g: Le pido que + subjunctive
‘Le pido que ... los fortalezca’ uses le for the person asked and los for the people to be strengthened; fortalezca is subjunctive.
e: con el poder que procede de sus gloriosas riquezas
Con names the empowering means, and the relative que procede de explains the power's source in God's glorious riches.

g: Para que + subjunctive, then participles
‘Para que ... habite’ states purpose. ‘Arraigados y cimentados’ then describes the plural recipients with agricultural and building imagery.
e: Cristo habite en sus corazones
Habitar is a durable ‘to dwell,’ stronger than a brief visit. En sus corazones places that dwelling in the recipients' inner lives.

g: Cuán + coordinated adjectives
‘Cuán ancho y largo, alto y profundo’ uses cuán to introduce the degree of four adjectives; es appears after the full series.
e: junto con todos los santos
Junto con means ‘together with.’ The singular form junto functions adverbially here and does not agree with the plural subject.

g: Relative clause followed by a purpose passive
‘Que sobrepasa nuestro conocimiento’ modifies amor; ‘para que sean llenos’ then uses subjunctive passive to state the desired result.
e: ese amor que sobrepasa nuestro conocimiento
Ese points back to the love just described. The relative clause creates a deliberate paradox: knowing a love that exceeds knowledge.

v: works effectively; is powerfully at work
g: Subjunctive in an unrestricted relative
‘Todo lo que podamos imaginarnos o pedir’ uses subjunctive podamos because the scope is open-ended: anything we might imagine or ask.
e: Al que puede hacer muchísimo más
Al contracts a + el and introduces the one to whom the doxology is directed; muchísimo intensifies más beyond a simple comparison.

g: Sea for a doxological wish
‘A él sea la gloria’ uses present subjunctive sea in a formal wish: ‘to him be glory.’ The fronted a él identifies the recipient.
e: por los siglos de los siglos
This biblical superlative literally says ‘for the ages of the ages’ and idiomatically means ‘for ever and ever.’
